the Brown– Rho scaling of the masses of the mesons, the nucleon, and the axial coupling constant g A, is a natural way to introduce a scalar three-body force in the nuclear matter equation of state.
a self-consistent solution for the Fermi liquid theory of nuclear matter with the Brown–Rhoscaled interaction is in very good agreement with empirical values for nuclear properties.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the Babu– Brown induced interaction can be understood as a three-body interaction, and that Brown–Rho decimation can be understood as the inclusion of a scalar tadpole in the meson and the nucleon masses, which in turn can be understood as introducing a short-range, three-body force.
the Brown-Rho scaling of the masses of the mesons and the nucleons is a natural consequence of Landau Fermiliquid theory.

the Babu– Brown induced interaction, when combined with the Brown–RHO scaling of the nucleon and the meson masses, provides an effective description of nuclear matter, with the quasiparticles interacting through a low-momentum effective interaction.
